title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages, which work on the section conjecture for 'anabelian' fibrations over a higher-dimensional base). S is a normal (probably regular) connected base with function field K. U_S -> S is a tower of elementary fibrations. E_S, E_K and E_{U_S} etc. denote the corresponding fundamental groups (extensions of pi_1(S), resp. Gal(K)). A Galois section E_K -> E_{U_K} gives a rational section of U_K, and the question is whether this section is 'unramified over S'. On the previous page Grothendieck reduces the condition to codimension 1. By Zariski–Nagata purity, pi_1(S \ Y) = pi_1(S) for Y of codimension >= 2, so the kernel of E_K -> E_S equals the kernel of E_K -> E_{S'}, with S' = S \ Y. This kernel is generated by the kernels for a covering of S' by 'modular' opens S'_i.

This page draws the consequence. If the rational section is unramified over each S'_i, i.e. over S', then it should be unramified over S. Equivalently, one needs an a priori geometric extension property: a section of U_S over S' (complement of a closed set Z with codim(Z,S) >= 2) extends to a section over S.

Step by step ('de proche en proche') through the tower, the problem reduces to the case of a relative curve U_S = X_S - T. Here X is smooth over S of relative dimension 1 (implicitly proper) and T is finite étale over S. One may assume T is split over S (after an étale base change).

- Genus >= 1: Weil's extension theorem says a rational map into an abelian scheme (via the Abel–Jacobi embedding X -> Jacobian or Pic-torsor), defined in codimension 1, extends. Hence the section extends to a section s: S -> X. Let D = s^{-1}(T). It is an effective Cartier divisor on S, since T is a relative Cartier divisor. Its trace on S' = S \ Z is empty because the section lands in U over S'. Its support lies in Z of codimension >= 2, so by Krull's Hauptidealsatz D = 0. Hence s factors through U_S. 'OK.'

The genus 0 case is not treated on this page. There X = P^1 and T has >= 3 points, so U_S is affine over S. The extension then follows from algebraic Hartogs for normal S, but Grothendieck does not say this here. The next page returns to the local-ring / discrete-valuation-ring formulation (diagrams (9), (10)) and the aim of showing phi_x kills the inertia I_x.
errors: Genus 0 case (P^1 minus >= 3 points) not addressed on this page. It is easy: U_S is affine over S, so sections over S' extend by Hartogs for normal S. Still, it is a gap as written.

Hypotheses on S are implicit. Weil's extension theorem in the relative form (as in Bosch–Lütkebohmert–Raynaud) needs S normal (regular is safest). For genus >= 1 one also needs an embedding into a group scheme or torsor, e.g. Abel–Jacobi. A base point comes from T split and nonempty, or one uses a Pic^1-torsor étale-locally. Properness of X over S is assumed but not written.

The 'de proche en proche' dévissage tacitly uses that the extension property is stable under composition in the tower. This is true (extend the image in the intermediate level first, then base-change), but it is not stated.

ideas.what: Reduce unramifiedness of a birational (Galois) section over a higher-dimensional base to codimension 1, via purity of pi_1 plus an extension property for sections of anabelian fibrations across codimension >= 2.
ideas.modern_name: Zariski–Nagata purity; reduction of the relative section conjecture to discrete valuation rings / specialization of sections
ideas.usually_credited_to: Purity: Zariski–Nagata, SGA1 X / SGA2. Section-conjecture specialization arguments: Stix and others (2000s).
ideas.where_published: Purity is in SGA1 X.3 and SGA2. The relative section conjecture framework appears in Grothendieck's 1983 letter to Faltings, but not this specific argument.

ideas.what: Sections of a hyperbolic curve X - T over S \ Z (codim Z >= 2) extend over S. Genus >= 1 via Weil's extension theorem, then the pullback divisor of T is supported in codimension >= 2 and hence empty.
ideas.modern_name: Extension of morphisms into hyperbolic curves / polycurves across codimension 2 (Weil extension theorem; Néron-type extension property)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Weil (extension theorem for abelian varieties); relative form in Bosch–Lütkebohmert–Raynaud, Néron Models §4.4; used in work on hyperbolic polycurves (e.g. Hoshi, Mochizuki)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard technical reduction (purity plus Weil extension plus the Hauptidealsatz) within Grothendieck's working-out of a relative section conjecture. All ingredients are classical and the conclusion is known. It is of historical interest only, as evidence that Grothendieck treated the section conjecture over higher-dimensional bases with this dévissage.
transcription_corrections: 'est aussi signifie' should read approximately 'ce qui est aussi signifier' (an awkward phrase in the manuscript itself).
'[-...-] [-...-] ≈ T décomposé sur S': the struck-out words are followed by a symbol read as '≈'. This is more plausibly an abbreviation meaning 'on peut supposer' / 'et', i.e. 'T décomposé sur S'.
'$X$ lisse {+sur $S$,+}': the insertion 'sur S,' is written above the line, replacing a struck-out 'de'. The transcription is correct here.
